exact_statement: A positive Radon measure with positive finite local ball-mass exponent a at x has logarithmic disk potential T(R)=(1/pi) integral_{B(x,R)} log(R/|x-y|) mu(dy) with the same R exponent a.
reproduction: Tonelli yields pi*T(R)=integral_0^R mu(B(x,s)) ds/s. For any eta in (0,a), s^(a+eta)<=mu(B(x,s))<=s^(a-eta) at small s; integration sandwiches T between constants times R^(a+eta) and R^(a-eta).
remaining_gap: Converting Euclidean radius to the actual LQG metric radius still needs an independently known exponent.

exact_statement: For Euclidean Brownian motion on R^2 and snowflake metric |x-y|^theta with 0<theta<=1, metric Hausdorff dimension and mean-exit exponent are 2/theta while spectral dimension is 2.
reproduction: Metric r-ball has Euclidean radius r^(1/theta); Hausdorff diameter powers scale by theta; heat kernel remains (2*pi*t)^(-1) on diagonal. Solve (1/2)Delta u=-1 on Euclidean disk to get center mean exit R^2/2. For theta<1 every nonconstant path has infinite snowflake length by fine partitions.
remaining_gap: This is not a counterexample to the strong LQG length-metric axioms and gives no value of d_gamma.

assumptions: the stated positive distance exponent exists
reproduction: Divide the two limits log T(r)/log r and log delta(r)/log r; the common Q-alpha cancels. The denominator limit is positive.
remaining_gap: The actual LQG distance exponent is an assumption containing unknown xi, so the calculation cannot evaluate d_gamma.

exact_statement: For 0<gamma<2, the zero-boundary disk GFF circle-average GMC of planar Lebesgue measure has logarithmic disk potential exponent 2-gamma^2/2 at GMC-almost every interior point, almost surely; a positive continuous local weight preserves it.
assumptions: their log-covariance normalization and dyadic circle-average GMC
Lebesgue measure on disk is exact-dimensional with dimension 2
reproduction: Corollary 2.3 gives mu_gamma(B(x,r)) exponent 2-gamma^2/2 for mu_gamma-a.e. x. It is positive since gamma<2. Apply independently checked W519-L2; local upper/lower weight bounds preserve the exponent and null sets.
remaining_gap: This concerns Euclidean balls and their logarithmic potential, not LQG metric balls or sample exit times.

exact_statement: For 0<a<1, D^a is a topology-preserving metric and dim_H(X,D^a)=dim_H(X,D)/a; it preserves reduced scalar covariance after xi->a*xi but generally fails the LQG length-space axiom.
assumptions: only reduced scalar identities, no pathwise Weyl scaling
reproduction: Concavity gives the triangle inequality; diameter powers yield the Hausdorff identity. For any continuous path 0->1 in [0,1], first hitting times of levels k/n give path-length sum n*(1/n)^a=n^(1-a)->infinity. Thus no path has finite D^a length; scalar covariance remains only a weak countermodel.
remaining_gap: No alternative canonical LQG metric or exact d_gamma is obtained.

exact_statement: For 0<gamma<2, xi>0, Q=2/gamma+gamma/2 and alpha in [-2,2], F(alpha)=(2-alpha^2/2)/(xi*(Q-alpha)) has unique maximum gamma/xi at alpha=gamma.
assumptions: deterministic algebra; the cited metric thick-point theorem is for each fixed alpha almost surely
reproduction: Q-2=(2-gamma)^2/(2*gamma)>0. Multiplication by xi*(Q-alpha) gives gamma*Q-gamma*alpha-2+alpha^2/2=(alpha-gamma)^2/2. Equality is unique at alpha=gamma in the interval; F(+/-2)=0.
remaining_gap: xi=gamma/d_gamma is already an input, so maximizing F restates rather than evaluates d_gamma; no uncountable almost-sure or union-dimension inference is accepted.

exact_statement: On C, D_p(x,y)=|x-y|^p for 0<p<=1 has d=2/p; D_{p,c}=exp(gamma*p*c/2)D_p and mu_c=exp(gamma*c)H^d_{D_p} obey xi*d=gamma with xi=gamma*p/2.
assumptions: only constant-shift covariance, not strong LQG axioms
reproduction: The p-snowflake is a metric and transforms diameter powers, giving d=2/p. Multiplying D_p by exp(xi*c) multiplies H^d by exp(xi*d*c)=exp(gamma*c). For p<1 it is not a length metric by the all-path hitting-time proof.
remaining_gap: The construction does not determine the canonical random LQG metric dimension.
